results.releaseNotes:
NEW
- maverick (palette: processors > misc): an effect patched from ingredients of the other processors, three to five blocks with modulators and routings, assembled anew on each placement. new patch (edit view, top bar, left of randomize) assembles another; randomize redraws the values of the current one.
- drift (edit view, clock row, after x4): the node's clock wanders about the tempo and stalls at times, so its rhythm plays irregularly at the division chosen. Available on every voice except the sampled instruments.
- Custom scale (session settings > scale > custom): a keyboard of the twelve notes, each named; tap a note to add it to the scale or remove it. The scale follows the root note.
- AUv3 instrument and effect nodes: a level button (edit view, top bar, left of done) shows or hides the level slider, which sits below the plugin's interface on iPad and above it on iPhone.
- visualizer (palette: first section, beside synths and controllers): a node that draws animated visuals from the outlets joined to it; full screen lays them over the canvas, which stays operable beneath.

CHANGES
- convolve (palette: processors > misc) rebuilt: seven synthesized impulse responses, partitioned convolution, crossfaded on change.
- cz, formant (palette: generators): play one octave higher.
- bell (palette: generators): plays two octaves higher.
- Abstract guided path: draws no percussive or drum families, places every voice as a drone, and sets drift on each so a clock switched on plays irregularly.
- Angiogenesis never removes an AUv3 plugin node; it may still move and randomize it.
- maverick fades out after the transport stops.
- visualizer: preset changes blend without a pause.

FIXES
- AUv3 plugins: opening a plugin's edit view for the first time no longer causes an audio dropout.
- iPhone: the keyboard stays up when a name field is selected in the save and rename dialogs.
- Undo after creating a patch restores the previous patch's tempo and key.
- Automatic processes (angiogenesis, patch creation, expansion) no longer display refused-connection marks on the canvas.
- maverick: the filter block could sustain a square-wave tone with no input; it stays within its stable range.
- maverick: new patch starts a new instrument, so the chain heard matches the one shown.
results.description:
Vascular is a canvas-based electroacoustic instrument. Create sound generators and processors by touching the canvas, then connect them to build the signal path. Moving a node changes its stereo position, while each node provides its own synthesis, processing, modulation and rhythmic controls.

FEATURES

- 55 synthesis families, including subtractive, FM, additive, granular, spectral, physical modelling, wavetable, wave-terrain, pulsar and stochastic synthesis.
- 3 macrosynths, complete synthesizers in a single node: resurgent (2 scenes, 3 oscillators, 2 filters, effects), bayarea, a West Coast voice, and poundhard, an FM drum voice from kicks to industrial percussion.
- A complete DX7 implementation.
- Holos, a special node that combines elements and parameters from other nodes to create a new semi-modular synthesizer instantly.
- A sample player for loading your own loops, with time-stretching, forward and reverse playback, stuttering, splicing and tape-style manipulation derived from classic electroacoustic techniques.
- Sampled acoustic instruments that generate melodic loops in the session's tonal key.
- Drum synthesis, a 303, a 16-oscillator supersaw and live granular processing.
- Microphone input for processing external sound.
- 71 processors, including filters, distortion, delays, combs, phasing, diffusion, reverb, spectral freezing, convolution, pitch tracking, harmony, vocoding, spectral delays, tape loops and broken-media effects.
- Host your own AUv3 instruments, effects and MIDI plugins as nodes on the canvas, their settings kept with your sessions (in-app purchase).
- 7 controllers that play or move other nodes: a melodic sequencer with a piano-roll editor; an arpeggiator that turns a single arpeggio into a fugue across up to 6 voices; a drum machine with fills and breaks; a shift register; bouncing cars whose collisions are notes; a Game of Life swept by a playhead; and an LFO controller with 3 LFOs on each of up to 6 nodes.
- Kick side chains with adjustable depth, and a master bus compressor.
- An effects sequencer with 4 lanes of any processor, each with its own length.
- A randomizer that creates whole patches, transforms what is on the canvas, expands it or dismantles it, and deals or removes LFOs, gates and motifs.
- A padlock on every parameter, keeping it out of reach of the randomizer and every LFO.
- Mute and solo: tap a node to mute it, hold it to hear it alone with its chain.
- Angiogenesis, which moves nodes, rewires connections, adds processors and changes their parameters automatically. It never removes your voices, cuts a controller's connections or modifies microphone nodes.
- Adjustable mutation rate and automatic adaptation to the processing capacity of the device.
- A shared session clock with tap tempo and an independent clock division for each rhythmic source.
- 27 scales from 4 musical traditions, plus microtonal tunings imported from Scala files.
- Guided paths for restricting generators and processors to a selected musical territory.
- A searchable palette, in alphabetical order, with favourites.
- Rebalance, which spreads the outputs evenly across the whole stereo field.
- A multilayer gesture looper.
- 32 pattern slots with adjustable morphing between complete instrument states.
- Sessions that store the network, settings and tonal key together.
- 48 levels of undo and redo.
- Recording, playback, renaming and sharing of takes.
- A transport that stops active sound sources while allowing effect tails to decay naturally.

AUV3

Vascular also runs as an AUv3 instrument in AUM, Loopy Pro, Logic and other compatible hosts, and follows the host's tempo and transport.

The interface runs full-screen in landscape orientation and is operated directly with your fingers. The main buttons remain along the top of the display, away from the hand interacting with the canvas.
